answer: A reef mints zephyrs only for work it commissioned and re-ran on its own silicon, a float fixed at W per epoch, and grants an agent's next signal only when that agent burns one zephyr. A clone's fabricated epoch fails the re-run, so it earns none; the operator must buy k zephyrs each epoch from honest earners, and its own k-wide bid lifts the price it pays to p·W/(W−k) — a recurring bill, steeper with every clone, that no wallet-splitting dodges, since impact tracks total volume. A newcomer earns its zephyr with one judged epoch.
